predecessors.name: Confederation of the Rhine
predecessors.text: the surviving German states of the Confederation of the Rhine, whose members the Congress of Vienna regrouped with Austria and Prussia

successors.name: North German Confederation
successors.text: 'incorporating all the German states north of the Main River' (Austro-Prussian War page)

ledger.x: 8 June 1815: the German Confederation is founded.
June 1815: Luxembourg enters the Confederation under the King of the Netherlands.
1818: the Duchies of Auschwitz and Zator are included in the Confederation.
1839: 'the larger province of Luxembourg had left the Confederation at its accession to Belgium in 1839' (German Confederation page; no month given).
5 September 1839: the Duchy of Limburg joins the Confederation.
11 April 1848: East and West Prussia and much of Posen are admitted to the Confederation.
19 April 1848: Prussian troops cross into Schleswig for the Confederation's federal war.
1850: 'the Duchies of Auschwitz and Zator, parts of the Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria, were only included from 1818 to 1850.'
30 May 1851: the restored Diet removes East and West Prussia and Posen.
8 May 1852: the second London Protocol ends the First Schleswig War.
24 December 1863: 'Saxon and Hanoverian troops marched into Holstein on behalf of the Confederation' (the federal execution, Bundesexekution; Second Schleswig War page).
The Second Schleswig War page does not say when the federal execution ended.
15 June 1866: Prussia invades Hanover, Saxony and the Electorate of Hesse.
23 August 1866: the German Confederation is dissolved.

wars.name: First Schleswig War
wars.outcome: Danish victory, 'Status quo ante bellum' (infobox 24 March 1848 - 8 May 1852); the Confederation's only federal war (Bundeskrieg).

wars.name: Second Schleswig War
wars.outcome: The Confederation 'took no part, as Schleswig was not a member'; it had ordered federal execution against Holstein in 1863 and Austria and Prussia then declared war on Denmark.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Prussian victory: 'Dissolution of the German Confederation', exclusion of Austria from German affairs; Prussia annexed Hanover, Holstein, Schleswig, Hesse-Kassel, Nassau and Frankfurt (infobox).

certainty.note: Membership followed crown-land and state boundaries fixed by the Final Act and the Federal Act; no territory of its own.
